reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports HfO2 formation and reduced oxidation on a VZrHfNbTa HEA substrate, but the hypothesis applies this to a different substrate (Zr-alloy cladding) and service environment (steam oxidation in LOCA) without direct evidence. The key premise that the mechanism translates to Zr-alloys is unsupported, and the specific coating method and steam conditions are not validated by E1.
premises: A hafnium coating on a refractory high-entropy alloy forms a dense HfO2 protective layer during high-temperature oxidation.
This HfO2 layer reduces oxidation weight gain compared to an uncoated sample.
The coating process (hot-press sintering) can produce a ~120 μm thick hafnium coating.
The coating remains effective at temperatures around 1600 °C.
The protective mechanism (HfO2 barrier reducing oxygen diffusion) will translate to a zirconium-alloy substrate.
